## §3 — What went wrong

- ⚠️ **F-AUDB-1 — matrix row 191 paperwork mismatch.** The implementer flipped `_concept-audit-matrix.md` row 191 ("Session tag vocabulary") from `partially-honored` → `honored` despite plan §2 row 1 (`plan.md:145`) + plan claim 16 (`plan.md:780`) explicitly requiring it to **stay** `partially-honored` (split-axis: immutability honored, emission still aspirational). Audit B iter 1 caught it cleanly with an actionable Trivial-multi recommendation; orchestrator re-spawned implementer; Audit B iter 2 confirmed GREEN. Root cause: implementer treated all matrix rows in §2 as binary `honored / not-honored` without re-reading the plan's explicit per-row target column for split-axis cases. Gap-closing change in §5.
- ⚠️ **Cascade over-prediction (favourable but unmodelled).** Planner predicted ~10–15 sites for `RepositoryError::` exhaustive matches needing `From<...>` cascade; actual 0 needing edits. Same pattern observed CH-09 + CH-11: production callers consistently use `other =>` catch-all + `From<RepositoryError>` → HTTP 500/422 conversions, so additive variants don't trigger compile cascade. Three-cycle confirmation makes this an established cross-cycle pattern (see §6); standards update in §5.
- ⚠️ **F5.B initial planner cost estimate was 10× the actual.** Iter 1 planner cited "+1 day estimated, +1 migration column for audit_event family" for F5.B. User locked F5.B; iter 2 planner re-investigation found audit_events schema is free-form (`event_type TYPE string`, `diff FLEXIBLE TYPE object`, `audit_class` already accepts `"alerted"`), reducing actual cost to +0.1d with **no migration**. Caught at iter 2 before approval — but if user had not pushed back on F5.A, the deferred-but-reachable security-event audit would have been silently lost. Codify a "user-lock divergence triggers planner re-verification of auto-approval criteria" rule in §5.
- ⚠️ **Audit B verified-header line drift (non-finding).** Audit A iter 1 noted plan claim 19 cited `AuditClass` at `audit/mod.rs:39` but actual location is line 36 (3-line drift, no semantic gap). Not a FAIL — but it indicates planner is line-citing from in-flight reading rather than a final-pre-publish re-grep. Optional standards refinement (low priority).
- ❌ **No production callsite for the audit-event builder yet.** F5.B ships the builder + 4 unit tests + 3 integration tests; the actual `audit.emit(frozen_tag_write_rejected(...))` call wires when a future chunk adds `update_session_tags`. The Repository trait docstring documents the contract, but discipline depends on the future-chunk planner reading + honoring it. If they don't, the builder is dead code. Tracking discipline-check via §6 open question Q3 + §5 standards row.
